children: Bitcoin faces 3 tests in a holiday-shortened week. Inflation data lands Wednesday, US stock markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving, and a $6.6 billion options expiry settles Friday.
Most bearish bets in that expiry already pay out at current prices. Spot Bitcoin ETF holders, meanwhile, get fewer trading hours than usual.

image.alt: 3 Events That Could Move Bitcoin Price in Thanksgiving Week

children: Wednesday’s Inflation Report Shapes December’s Fed Hike
The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index is the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge. Forecasts put October’s core PCE inflation,
at 3.2%, up from September.
Traders already price a December Fed rate hike as certain. Wednesday’s report mainly shapes the size of that move.
Fed Governor Christopher Waller has floated an extreme half-point hike. A hotter core reading would strengthen his case.
Higher rates also raise the cost of holding assets that pay no yield, such as Bitcoin.
Thursday’s holiday then takes US funds out of the market for a day.
Thanksgiving Leaves Bitcoin ETFs Dark for a Day
The New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) closes for Thanksgiving on Thursday and shuts at 1 p.m. ET on Friday. US spot Bitcoin ETFs follow the same schedule.
Bitcoin keeps trading through the holiday while the funds sit idle.
The funds head into the break with heavy redemptions behind them. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have shed more than $3.5 billion so far in November, SoSoValue data shows.
BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust
led the exodus with a
on November 19.
Friday’s options expiry settles at 08:00 UTC, before that half-session begins.
Options Traders Want Bitcoin Price to Drop
Bitcoin trades near $59,000, after seeing a modest recovery over the past 24 hours.
Meanwhile, data from Deribit shows that around 112,000 Bitcoin options contracts expire on Friday. That’s roughly a quarter of all active Bitcoin options on the exchange.
So, what does this mean for Bitcoin’s price?
Options allow traders to bet on whether Bitcoin will rise or fall. Currently, the data shows that bearish bets are in a much stronger position.
Bets on falling prices (puts): Nearly 75% are already above their target levels, meaning they have value at today’s price. The biggest groups are at $70,000 and $75,000.
Bets on rising prices (calls): Almost all need Bitcoin to recover significantly before they have value. The largest group is at $90,000.

Deribit’s max pain price is $73,000. This is the level where options buyers would collectively lose the most money at expiry. However, Bitcoin is trading far below it, making that level less useful for predicting Friday’s price.
With three major events approaching this week, analysts have already warned that Bitcoin could fall further toward $50,000–$54,000.

title: 3 Events That Could Shake Bitcoin Prices During Thanksgiving Week
